desc:
Cut the array nums into exactly k consecutive non-empty groups. The score of a group is the remainder of the sum of its elements when divided by p. Return the largest possible total score (the sum of the k group scores).

nums = [3,5,7], k = 2, p = 10  -> 15   ([3,5] scores 8, [7] scores 7)
nums = [4,6,5], k = 2, p = 5   -> 5    ([4] scores 4, [6,5] has sum 11 and scores 1)
hints: Work with prefix sums reduced modulo p. A group that spans positions t .. i-1 scores (pre[i] - pre[t]) mod p.

Let dp[j][i] be the best total score for the first i elements cut into j groups. The last group starts at some t, so you maximize dp[j-1][t] + (pre[i] - pre[t]) mod p over t. Trying every t is too slow.

The only thing about t that matters besides dp[j-1][t] is the residue pre[t], and there are only p residues. For each residue keep the best dp[j-1][t] seen so far, and for every i scan the p residues.
editorial: Let pre[i] be the prefix sum of the first i elements modulo p. A group t .. i-1 has score (pre[i] - pre[t]) mod p, so dp[j][i] = max over t of dp[j-1][t] + (pre[i] - pre[t]) mod p. A direct scan over t costs O(n2 · k).

The score depends on t only through pre[t], a value in 0..p-1. So for each layer we keep an array best[r] holding the largest dp[j-1][t] among the starts t already seen with pre[t] = r. For a new end i we scan the p residues and take the maximum of best[r] + (pre[i] - r) mod p. The start t = i - 1 is added to best just before processing i. Total time O(n · k · p), memory O(n).
